## TL;DR

The Homebrew "Updating" signal now reads only the tap's formula-update workflow, `repoos-release.yml` ("Update RepoOS formula"), not any tap run. It counts only that workflow's `repository_dispatch` runs that started inside the viewed release's window. Unrelated tap CI can no longer make an out-of-sync row read Updating. The release banner was already scoped to `release.yml`. One requirement from the freeze cannot be met as written: the tap's run list carries no version or tag, so the match is by time window, not by tag or version. I checked this against the live tap with `gh api`, not just the docs.

## Work and rationale

The round-2 check listed the tap's last ten runs of any kind. The freeze asks for the tap's formula-update workflow, matched to the viewed tag or version. The repo does not record that workflow's file, so I looked at the real tap through `gh api repos/repo-os/homebrew-tap/actions/workflows`. "Update RepoOS formula" is `.github/workflows/repoos-release.yml`. Its recent runs are all `repository_dispatch` with `display_title` `repoos-release`.

That display title is the problem for version matching. The Actions list response does not include the dispatch payload (`client_payload.version`, which the release workflow sends), and the title is only the event name. Nothing in the list identifies which release a run is for. I did not fake a version match. The closest scope the API supports is file, plus event, plus time window.

`homebrewTapUpdateInProgress` now calls `actions/workflows/repoos-release.yml/runs?event=repository_dispatch`. It still checks the event, the active status and the `created_at` window client-side, so the logic holds even if the server ignored the query. The window comes from the viewed release's run, unchanged from round 2. If there is no release run, the tap is not queried. The file name is a constant with a comment, not a config key. A config key would need a Settings control and schema entry, which the freeze did not ask for.

The callers at the tap-set and `applyHomebrewUpdatingState` lines need no change. They still take a per-repository boolean, and only the query behind it changed.

## Approaches tried

I looked for the version in the run's jobs and steps. The job list does not expose the payload either, so reading the version would mean fetching logs, which is too heavy for a per-check signal. I also considered asking the tap to put the version in its run name. That would be a change in the tap repository, outside this task, so I recorded it as the way to get an exact match rather than doing it here.

## Challenges and blockers

The freeze asks for a match to the tag or version. That is not achievable from the runs list. I am handing off with the scoped version and stating the gap in the report. If the human wants an exact match, the options are the tap setting its run name to include the version, or the check reading the dispatch payload. Either is a follow-up.

Tests: the helper now serves two endpoints. The formula-update workflow endpoint returns the tap runs under test. The repo-wide `actions/runs` endpoint returns unrelated tap CI. The new case puts a push run and an unrelated dispatch run in progress on the repo-wide list, with nothing active on the formula-update workflow, and expects out-of-sync. The test also asserts the scoped URL was requested. If the query reverted to the repo-wide list, the unrelated dispatch would match the window and the test would fail. The no-anchor case asserts that no request reaches any tap Actions endpoint.

Docs: `docs/releases.md` names `repoos-release.yml` and says the match is by time window, not by tag. The earlier note that an unset `release.workflow` disables the banner, the grace window and the tap query is still there.

## Key learnings

The Actions list endpoints are the wrong place to match a version. Those responses carry event, status, path, times and a title, but not the dispatch payload. Matching on something the list does not carry leads to a check that quietly never fires. Check the real data before writing a matcher.

A test that serves the same answer from every endpoint cannot detect a query on the wrong endpoint. The mock has to serve unrelated data from the endpoint the bug would hit.

## Verification

`bun run fmt` ran before the tests. `bun run test` over `distribution.test.ts` and `releases-distribution-view.test.ts` passed 55 of 55 and 57 of 57. The scoped `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` ran in the background and its result is recorded in the handoff. No live tap call was made by the code. The `gh api` calls were read-only and only confirmed the tap's workflow file and run shape.
